sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Our older Dortmund data covers only a few garages and stops in 2022–2023, so we show no recent trend. It does show how hard Covid hit: the garages we then measured stood at 14% occupied in April 2020 and 23% in January 2021, and pedestrian counts on Westenhellweg fell from 3,472 an hour in January 2020 to 581 a year later [16]. The occupancy figures below are for weekdays and weekends in August and September 2026.

Dortmund has used price first. On-street fees were raised on 1 August 2023, the first adjustment in more than 20 years, from €1.50 to €2.50 an hour in the centre and along the Wall ring [1], and central streets have been chargeable on Sundays since about 2023 [3]. The city had proposed more moderate rises at its own garages (DOPARK) [0]. Road space is the next step. In December 2022 the council approved a three-stage rebuild of the Wall ring that removes one lane per direction, with full reconstruction not expected before 2030 [4]. In January 2025 the city proposed bus lanes in front of the main station, which the council was to decide in February [5]. Residents' parking is being extended slowly: in May 2026 the council set a schedule of two new zones a year, with planning running to 2032 [6].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
DOPARK is the city's parking company, with an outside shareholder [11]. A renewed central guidance system was due to start in August 2022, passing free-space data to the national mobility marketplace, with barriers planned at four park-and-ride sites [7][8]. The city also publishes the availability of centre garages and park-and-ride sites as open data every ten minutes [9]. The Konzerthaus garage was renovated from August 2022 and available again by October 2024, late and with a cost framework of about €4 million after asbestos and fire-safety problems [10]; it now has two 22 kW charging points [12]. In 2019 the utility DEW21 won EU funding for six fast-charging points in the Mitte district, but the report does not say whether they are in garages [13].

Retail is the main pressure on the centre. The Galeria Kaufhof store on Westenhellweg closed in August 2024, while the Karstadt store was kept open [14][15]. In our data the garage beside the Karstadt store, Hansaplatz/Karstadt, averages 29% on weekdays.

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
Dortmund's garages are cheap and mostly quiet. DOPARK's five central garages, about 1,700 spaces, charge €1.80 an hour and €14 a day, 13% below their neighbours, and average 21% on weekdays. DIAG's three garages around the Hauptbahnhof and the Friedensplatz charge €2 and run at 37%, Contipark's two (Kuckelke and Bissenkamp) charge €3 and run at 35%, and the Dortmunder U (Goldbeck) and Thier-Galerie garages, at €2, at 25% and 23%. So here the dearer garages are the fuller ones. DOPARK's Rathaus/Stadtgarten garage is almost empty at weekends (4%).

The fullest car park is the small Alte Post at the NH Hotel (63%), followed by the park-and-ride at the Westfalenpark (58%) and the St.-Johannes-Hospital garage, at €2.50 an hour (48%). Overall the city's garages are 31% occupied on weekdays and 21% at weekends, because many serve offices and clinics. Garages within 500 m of the Alter Markt average 30%, as do those 500 m–1 km out, and the nine around the main station 29%.
